meta.title: Buying a Stock Caps Your Loss at 100%. Shorting Doesn't.
meta.hook: When you buy a stock, you can lose 100%. When you short one, there's no ceiling on how much you can lose.
meta.description: Short selling means borrowing shares, selling them, and aiming to buy them back cheaper. Because a stock's price has no upper limit, losses on a short position are theoretically unlimited — unlike buying, where the most you can lose is your original investment. Educational content only, not financial advice.

scenes.narration: When you buy a stock, the most you can lose is everything you put in.

scenes.narration: Short selling means borrowing shares, selling them, and hoping to buy them back cheaper later.

scenes.narration: If the price drops, you pocket the difference. Simple enough.

scenes.narration: But if the price rises instead, you still have to buy those shares back, at whatever price the market demands.
